title: Penske Logistics to Cut 89 Laredo Jobs as Vallecillo Road Facility Closes March 1

content:
Penske Logistics will permanently lay off 89 workers at its Laredo facility on Vallecillo Road, with the closure set to take effect March 1, according to layoff notices the company filed with the Texas Workforce Commission.

The Laredo cuts are part of a wider round of Texas logistics layoffs announced just before Thanksgiving. Penske Logistics and CPC Logistics together plan to eliminate 369 jobs across the state, the notices show.

In El Paso, Penske said about 110 employees at its facility at 48 Walter Jones Boulevard will be permanently laid off after changes by a customer led to that site's closure. Penske said it has provided warehousing services at both the El Paso and Laredo locations for several years and is working to manage the transition.

In Waxahachie, CPC Logistics plans to end operations at a Walgreens distribution center, affecting about 170 commercial drivers. CPC Special Logistics South reported 17 planned layoffs and CPC Special Logistics West listed 153. The company said Walgreens is canceling its contracts with CPC at the distribution center, and operations there are expected to end on or around January 30, 2027.

The notices state the closures are permanent and that affected workers do not have bumping or automatic reemployment rights. CPC said employees may apply for open positions at other CPC locations, although the company said it cannot currently provide job placement assistance.

Most of the job losses are scheduled to begin after the holiday season. For Laredo, the loss of 89 warehouse jobs on Vallecillo Road lands in a sector that has long been one of the city's steadiest employers — and it raises the question of what happens next for those workers, and whether other warehouses along the corridor will absorb them.

Sources: Texas Workforce Commission layoff notices, via NewsChunks, Nov. 27, 2026.
